claims.statement: Pi Agent Desktop is a pure Electron app with no internal HTTP server and no bundled Node runtime (package.json engines >=22.19.0 <23; main is out/main/main.js).
npm run dev (scripts/dev.mjs) starts a Vite dev server on localhost:5173, a tsup watch loop building main/preload/host into out/, and launches Electron, tearing down the full process tree on exit.
npm run lint (ESLint --max-warnings=0), npm run typecheck (two tsc projects), and npm test (node --test src/**/*.test.mjs with a 120s default timeout) are the local development quality checks.

npm run verify (scripts/verify.mjs) is the single release gate running format, lint, typecheck, dependency contract, unit tests, managed-process and security/contract checks, build, artifact isolation, and smoke/e2e tests, aborting on the first failure.
npm run build outputs out/main+preload+agent-host via tsup and out/renderer via Vite; npm run pack and npm run dist route through scripts/package-desktop.mjs to electron-builder (--dir vs release).

Packaged Windows installer is named Pi-Agent-Desktop-Unsigned-Beta-Setup until Authenticode signing is provisioned; macOS dmg/zip and Linux AppImage are built by electron-builder (electron-builder.yml).

RPC methods are typed in src/contract/api.ts (Api + Streams), implemented in src/agent-host/handlers.ts, and called from the renderer through src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts; components never touch MessagePort directly.

Toolchain capabilities, providers, preferences, health and error codes are defined in src/shared/toolchains/types.ts; the scan/selection pipeline is src/main/toolchains/manager.ts and install/repair is src/main/toolchains/installer.ts.

Browser authorization, permissions, leases and confirmations are enforced entirely in src/main/browser/ and driven by the renderer via piBridge.browser*; coding permissions never imply browser rights.

scripts/check-desktop-security.mjs is the compile-time security gate asserted by verify.mjs; changes to security invariants require updating both the checker and the source, then running check:desktop-security and verify.
